t.E924a.agn: In 1992, following new data showing that bromate residues are present even in bread made from flour treated at previously acceptable levels, JECFA concluded that the use of potassium bromate as a flour treatment agent is not appropriate and evaluated the substance as a genotoxic carcinogen; it reiterated this view in 1995. In 1999 IARC classified potassium bromate in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans), based on sufficient evidence in experimental animals and inadequate evidence in humans; kidney and thyroid tumours have been reported in animals.
t.E924a.eff.0.a: Even at the residue levels remaining in baked bread
t.E924a.eff.0.t: Kidney and thyroid tumours have been reported in animals; JECFA evaluated it as a genotoxic carcinogen and found its use as a flour treatment agent not appropriate; IARC classifies it in Group 2B
t.E924a.eval: Not authorised as a flour treatment agent in the EU. In 1992 JECFA found its use as a flour treatment agent not appropriate. In 1999 IARC classified it in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic). In the US, California is banning it from 1 January 2027 under AB 418.
t.E924a.found.0: Not on the EU list of authorised additives
t.E924a.prod: Produced chemically by passing bromine into potassium hydroxide solution or by electrolysis.
t.E924a.regx.0: Use as a flour treatment agent is not acceptable (1992, reiterated in 1995); it was noted that residues may remain in bread.
t.E924a.regx.1: Group 2B: possibly carcinogenic to humans (Monograph Volume 73).
t.E924a.regx.2: It was stated that bromate should not be added to flour.
t.E924a.summary: A strong flour improver. Was used to strengthen bread dough.
t.E924a.what: Has been used as a flour treatment agent added to flour to improve dough properties.
